score_notes.retention: The spine loop now closes at 91% ('Point, you.' 55.82 s of 61.5). The win was moved to round 5, and every round before it is a spoken loss, so 'which one, and how?' stays open through the back half. The rule 'Bigger wins.' is stated at 7.0 s, and every round ends on a spoken 2-word verdict stamp, with 'and/so' bridges into the next round. The ladder climbs: just longer than you -> 5 of you -> 35 of you -> 230 of you. After that the comparison flips to the round where you are bigger. Comedy: 'part of it is snot' (round 2) and 'tomorrow it's hungry again' (the peak). A false-reassurance turnstile at 41-44% has a background change at 45%. Remaining risks: the ROUND 1 card lands at 7.95 s but the spoken 'Round one' at 8.27 s (the Kokoro sentence pause cannot be removed). 'You' is in 50% of sentences (all 11 full content sentences, but none of the 11 stamp or title fragments).
score_notes.reference: The references were swapped to match the devices actually used. FLY (counted inventory, conjunction bridges, loop frame) and PUFFER (false-reassurance turnstile at 46%, deadpan deflations, the 60 s skeleton) are Shorts. SWALLOW supplies the scoring rule (0:14), verdict stamps (1:12) and the myth-bust 'Nope.' (5:39), and closes its title loop at 92%, which matches our 91%. PRESSURE is cited for its two devices only: the landmark shown and not said, and the planted word paid twice. Every alignment row was rechecked against research/corpus/explainer/<id>.md timestamps. The 76 s / 40-word rounds became 61.5 s / 19-36-word rounds (~8-11 s each). Raw values are on screen only, and the VO speaks only the 'N of you' form. Held at 8: 61.5 s is still past the 59 s corpus maximum. That is deliberate, because it keeps TikTok Creator Rewards eligibility (>60 s).
score_notes.originality: The gate passes against research/corpus + research/library/transcripts, and separately against episodes/ (the sibling pilot). The sibling overlap is gone: no heart, tongue, 2 bpm, gulp/pouch, throat ring or dinner plate. The aorta is compared to a basketball, which is also the payoff of the court plant. sibling_check was rewritten to say what is still shared (length as the anchor, daily food as a topic) and how it differs. Fact sourcing is corrected. Calf numbers are cited to Guinness/SeaWorld as widely cited estimates, not to NOAA. Daily food uses Savoca et al. 2021 (16 t), with NOAA's older 6 t noted. The aorta wording holds for any published width from ~17 to ~40 cm. Held at 8 because the aorta width still has no primary (ROM-published) measurement, and the flipper length is a proportion-based estimate. The VO claims are worded to hold across both ranges.
score_notes.producibility: A storyboard was generated from the measured TTS (gen_storyboard.py, all times anchored to spoken words). It validates (zod, Node 22 on the Spark). check_storyboards.py reports 'ready': every component is registered, every audio file exists, and the longest hold is 2.9 s. Ten stills were rendered on the Spark and checked (out/stills/bw_scale.jpg, bw_scale_fix.jpg). No new kit components are needed. The flipper, x-ray bones, spout, whale back, court, CountGrid, tunnel, basketball, bust and stinger icons are inline svg/core layers. Every SFX maps to an existing file. Every pxPerM is stated per shot (36 / 300 / 110 / calf 30 vs scene 120 / 2000). Held at 8 because the art is first-pass and needs one look-dev pass: the bust and ring motion, the Diver reading small at 47.8 s, and the krill 'pile' being a single big krill figure on the Balance. No MP4 has been rendered yet.
